- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >85), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward bias correction in next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≥0.4) and prices are falling, model underestimates drop — increase downward forecast bias, especially if recent history shows volatility.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for first 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows a clear reversal (e.g., from positive to negative), model often lags — anticipate and adjust forecast downward 2–3 days ahead.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon when sentiment is flat — model should not overfit recent trends; use 10–15 day moving average as baseline.
